doc.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First hearing Coleman Hawkins with Fletcher Henderson
summary: Hawkins's sound and chord sense at the Roseland stood out from the band; Shaw also recalls Bix with Whiteman.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Can you remember the first occasion you heard Coleman Hawkins?

I think it was Fletcher [Henderson] at the Roseland Ballroom. I remember him. I remember Tricky Sam [Nanton]. I can’t remember a lot about that band. I didn’t . . . The band didn’t impress me much. But when the Hawk played, or Bean, as they called him, that was a whole new thing. He had great chord sense . . . Now, today, that’s nothing, but in that day . . . One Hour, Jesus, what he did with that If I could be with you one hour tonight. It was remarkable. Bix was always around. When he was with [Paul] Whiteman, Sweet Sue and Changes and some of those records, they were remarkable. Dardenelle, what he did with that.
